scope: Passive research claims; not executable signals or permission for CAN transmission.

hypotheses.description: Bit changes with the recorded exterior-light ON/OFF pair; exact lamp/status meaning unconfirmed.
hypotheses.next_test: Repeat at least three cycles in another session; distinguish parking lights, manual low beam, AUTO mode without illumination, and automatic illumination. Mark actual lamp state separately from selector position.

hypotheses.description: Bit follows the same light pair; it may participate in IPC illumination state rather than encode a brightness value.
hypotheses.next_test: Separate lamp ON/OFF from brightness changes; keep lamps steady while adjusting brightness, then repeat with manual/AUTO selection.

hypotheses.description: Exploratory step has 0->1 at the light-ON marker and 1->0 at OFF, matching BH 0x354 byte 3 bit 6. This does not establish a common decoder for both buses.
hypotheses.next_test: Repeat independently and compare manual lamps, AUTO selection, actual illumination and beam/fog states.

hypotheses.description: Historical park-brake interpretation agrees with the explicit parking-brake pair about 0.8-0.9 s after markers; earlier generic brake markers also overlap transitions.
contradictions: Generic brake labels do not distinguish EPB operation from brake-pedal use; no independent actuator-state reference was captured.
hypotheses.next_test: Record pedal-only cycles with EPB unchanged, then EPB-only transitions while maintaining pedal pressure. Mark button operation and completed actuator state separately. Inspect C2 separately.

hypotheses.description: Window actions are present but no window field is identified. Raw bit steps include many unrelated candidates and mixed driver/passenger annotations.
contradictions: Event 26 describes driver-window closing and notes passenger-window opening. Only one explicitly driver-open marker; movement duration and final positions are unknown.
hypotheses.next_test: Stationary: driver down/up three times, then passenger down/up separately. Mark switch press, release and full-open/full-closed states; keep other controls and ignition steady.

hypotheses.description: Constant prefix 00 00 00 20 60 00 followed by a 4-bit rolling counter (byte 6, modulus 16) and its check byte (byte 7). Carries no payload state; candidate bits on it are phase artefacts (bundle top hits are here).
contradictions: 2026-10-23 raw re-analysis: byte 3 is 0xA5 in all five observed Race entries, 0x20 with LKA enabled outside Race, and 0x00 with manually disabled LKA in D. The claim that the whole payload carries no state is false. Counter/checksum exclusion still applies to bytes 6/7; see DNA-RELATED-4AE-001.
hypotheses.next_test: Preserve the counter/checksum finding; investigate byte 3 independently of counter phase. See docs/research/20261023-dna-selector.md.

hypotheses.description: Constant prefix 80 00 followed by a 4-bit rolling counter (byte 2) and a check byte (byte 3). Carries no payload state.
hypotheses.next_test: Same counter exclusion as COUNTER-HEARTBEAT-001.

hypotheses.description: Bytes 6-7 are a 4-bit counter and its check byte; bytes 0-5 carry drive-mode state. Only byte 6/7 candidates are spurious.
hypotheses.next_test: Restrict 0x5A8 candidate scoring to bytes 0-5.

hypotheses.description: Bytes 0-3 hold two 16-bit values that decrease monotonically and bytes 4-7 are constant (ff ff 00 00); it may be an accumulator/heartbeat rather than instantaneous state, which would make its window/seat-belt/mirror/suspension candidates drift.
contradictions: Automatic bit-step ranking shows moderate window/seat-belt/mirror/suspension agreement, but the field trend is monotonic.
hypotheses.next_test: Sample 0x341 over a quiet idle baseline and over a long steady interval; confirm whether the fields are time counters before accepting any state bit.

hypotheses.description: Closure/ajar status on the 10 ms backbone, gateway-duplicated on C2: boot at byte 2 bit 2 (active-low), bonnet at byte 3 bit 1 (active-low). Byte 6 is a counter and byte 7 a CRC.
contradictions: Single session; closure bits and other byte 0-3 activity are not yet separated.
hypotheses.next_test: Repeat boot-only and bonnet-only cycles and confirm the active-low sense with negative controls.

hypotheses.description: BH-side companion of 0x116; boot at byte 2 bit 2 follows the same open/closed sense.
hypotheses.next_test: Confirm it is the same body state as 0x116 in a repeated session.

hypotheses.description: Lock/door status byte: byte 3 carries 128 distinct values and its bits 2-6 follow lock/unlock; byte 6 is a counter and byte 7 a CRC.
hypotheses.next_test: Isolate lock, unlock and per-door open/close with the door warning marker.

hypotheses.description: High-volume backbone frame whose byte 0 takes single-bit values (0x20/0x40/0x80), suggesting a one-hot lamp/indicator flag; byte 7 is a CRC. The individual lamp was not isolated.
contradictions: Steady dipped/high/fog lamps produced no clean level bit; a pulse/one-hot encoding is plausible.
hypotheses.next_test: Activate one lamp at a time and read byte 0 raw values; keep lamps steady for several seconds.

hypotheses.description: Brake state lead on the 10 ms backbone: byte 2 bit 6 rises with the brake-pedal marker (ON 0.66 / OFF 0.01); 0x100 byte 0 also follows. Distinct from the 0x384 park-brake comment.
hypotheses.next_test: Pedal-only cycles with EPB unchanged, then EPB-only cycles with pedal held.

hypotheses.description: Byte 0 bit 4 rises with engine start and clears on stop (ON 0.83 / OFF 0.01). Conflicts with the existing reference-only note that calls 0x1FC active damping; both meanings may coexist on one multiplexed frame.
contradictions: Prior reference-only interpretation: active damping / differential status.
hypotheses.next_test: Repeat start/stop cycles and inspect the full payload to separate engine-running from the damping reference.

hypotheses.description: Historical hypothesis: BH 0x2F0 byte 4 bit 4 was proposed as a wiper-active status. The targeted three speed/off cycles contradict this mapping; the associated C1 0x736 and BH 0x46A HVAC leads remain separate unresolved observations.
contradictions: Rain sensor / wiper strokes were previously an explicit gap; this is a lead, not a decoder.

In 20261010-111025Z, byte 4 bit 4 occupancy across intermittent/slow/fast/off is 0.70/0/0.75/1.00 (run 1), 0/0.09/1.00/0 (run 2), and 0/0.22/1.00/1.00 (run 3). It remains high during some OFF windows and low during active ones; the apparent earlier correlation was a time-order/drift artefact. See docs/research/20261012-five-bundle-investigation.md.
hypotheses.next_test: If wiper state is still needed, record isolated stationary OFF/intermittent/slow/fast/washer states with long equal intervals and a physical lamp observation; investigate other frames without reusing 0x2F0 byte 4 bit 4.

hypotheses.description: Lane-keeping assist (LKA) is enabled/disabled by a double-click on the left stalk button (stationary, ignition on). The enable state is reported on the single-bit frame BH 0x4F6 byte 6 bit 1 (0 = disabled, 1 = enabled), gateway-duplicated on C2 0x547. Across the 2026-10-11 lane_assist_toggle recordings it tracked every one of the 12 toggles (two sessions, three OFF/ON cycles each) and also cleared whenever Race was engaged. The momentary button press is on C2 0x384 byte 3 bit 6 (and BH 0x5A0 byte 4 bit 0).
contradictions: The 2026-10-10 campaign planned the lane procedures on the assumption that LKA is toggled from a menu; the owner's confirmation of the left-stalk double-click supersedes that assumption.
hypotheses.next_test: Verify in the car that one C2 0x384 double-click sequence (press, release, press, release) from the firmware disables LKA, the original C2 0x547 / BH 0x4F6 reports remain OFF afterward, and a later driver double-click can re-enable it. Confirm the state bit against the dashboard lamp.

hypotheses.description: Drive mode (RDNA) code on the body broadcast 0x384 byte 1 bits 6..2 matches the firmware enum: N=0, D=2, A=4, Race=12. Confirmed from the 2026-10-11 dna_all_modes sessions (two sessions, three runs each, reversible against a Natural baseline). The same code is on BH 0x46C byte 7 bits 4..0; the dashboard frame BH 0x25A uses N=16, D=8, A=4, Race=1. These are recurring mode broadcasts. Rewriting one copy may influence listeners but has not been shown to change the body's stored mode.
contradictions: Raw re-analysis on 2026-10-23 found five successful Race entries across six marked attempts; 191050Z event 12 says Race but all recorded mode reports stay Dynamic until capture end. Event 1 in that session begins with Dynamic already selected. Original markers remain unchanged.

The owner subsequently reports that the installed one-shot default D briefly appears then returns to N (installed binary unknown). This is negative hardware evidence for persistence. Commit 80fdb13 corrects the CRC write and adds bounded state corroboration; no post-fix vehicle result yet.

All-session review 2026-10-23 supersedes the earlier absence-of-input finding: BH 0x256/DLC 4 reports 36 momentary direction pulses, each followed by the matching selector-associated mode change. This does not identify its physical transmitter or prove injected acceptance.
hypotheses.next_test: Vehicle acceptance of 00b4b99: bounded BH input gestures and actual sustained C1 DNA/transmission reports, including failure and physical-input priority.

hypotheses.description: Byte 1 bit 2 is the right direction-indicator active state. It follows three right ON/OFF cycles in 20261010-104325Z and two independent cycles in 20260928-204100Z; left-only markers are a negative control and hazard activates both 0x42D and 0x42E. The message is seen about every 100 ms while active; byte 2 low nibble rolls modulo 16 and byte 3 varies with it.
contradictions: Byte 0 uses different baseline codes (0x25/0x05 in October, 0x44/0x04 in September), so do not use whole-byte equality across sessions.
RX-only recordings do not establish whether this is a switch request, requested lamp state, or physical lamp feedback.
hypotheses.next_test: Confirm with independent physical right-lamp observation, and compare command timing with BH 0x46C and C2 0x73E.

hypotheses.description: Byte 1 bit 2 follows left direction-indicator active state in three October ON/OFF cycles; hazard activates it alongside 0x42D, right-only markers keep it clear. Symmetric layout to 0x42D, but only one independent left-side recording was found.
contradictions: A few frames remain high immediately after a left OFF marker, consistent with marker timing or release latency; this is not a blink-phase decoder.
RX-only capture does not prove physical lamp status or actuator command.
hypotheses.next_test: Repeat two left ON/OFF cycles in a separate stationary session with physical lamp observation; compare 0x42E byte 1 bit 2 to BH 0x46C and C2 0x73E.

hypotheses.description: The firmware J1850 payload CRC does not match any of 2,099 C1/C2 0x384 frames in the two October-11 DNA captures; byte 7 is always zero. The same algorithm matches all 286 C1 0x5A8 frames. The aa81111 default-mode rewrite invented a nonzero byte 7 on the observed layout. This does not establish ECU rejection or universality across vehicles. Commit 80fdb13 preserves byte 7; this source correction is not physical acceptance.
hypotheses.next_test: Install matched firmware and check whether factory D persists, the new result corroborates DNA/transmission, and the physical selector remains usable.

hypotheses.description: C1/C2 byte 0 correlates with settled N/A=0x50, D=0x40, Race=0x60 in both captures. Mode-dependent response; no evidence it is a selector command. Existing damping/differential reference interpretation remains unvalidated. Across all eight N-to-D edges it follows the local 0x384 by 12-27 ms on C1 and 13-27 ms on C2; median cadence is 20 ms. This strengthens the response interpretation, not the actuator identity.
hypotheses.next_test: Isolate damping/selector controls and establish the sender before assigning physical meaning.

hypotheses.description: C1/C2/BH byte 3 correlates with Race=0xA5, enabled LKA outside Race=0x20, and manually disabled LKA in Dynamic=0x00 in 190746Z. Its state content refutes the older all-counter claim; bytes 6/7 still roll/check. Individual bit meanings remain unresolved.
hypotheses.next_test: Separate Race and manual LKA changes; do not forge this byte as a mode request.

hypotheses.description: Byte 1 settles at N/A=0x00, D=0x10, Race=0x20 and can lag the known byte-0 mode field. This is not an identified knob press/release signal. Existing firmware only rewrites byte 0. Audit 2026-10-24: D button pulses repeatedly toggle byte1[5:4] between 1 (firm) and 0 (Soft), using the owner description to label calibration. Race entry shows 2; the implemented Mid=1 remains a candidate.

evidence.note: Context markers; exact transitions use original CAN frame IDs in the report, not nearest-marker labels.

hypotheses.next_test: Capture labelled Race Stiff -> Mid -> Stiff button actions and validate the inferred 2 -> 1 -> 2 field on BH 0x25A, plus injected startup acceptance.

hypotheses.description: Byte 1 is 0x07 during all five Race episodes and 0x9F outside Race in the DNA captures. Existing ACC status decoding uses byte 7; no physical meaning or control-command role is assigned to byte 1.
hypotheses.next_test: Correlate with independent ACC availability/status observations before interpreting byte 1.

hypotheses.description: Momentary selector direction: raw 0=released, 1=toward A (byte 0=20), 2=toward D/Race (byte 0=40). All 36 non-neutral pulses match selector-associated mode changes across three sessions. Every N-to-D (8/8) follows onset by 108-112 ms on BH; pulses last 154-294 ms. Five long holds precede Race by 1194-1211 ms. It is not a latched selected-mode report. C1 0x256/DLC 8 is unrelated. Startup replay implemented in 00b4b99; implementation does not promote the capture claim to hardware validated.

evidence.note: Original track_changed marker note mentions selecting D; it precedes the actual CAN transition by 23 seconds and supplies context only.

contradictions: An ignition-associated D-to-N reset has no selector pulse; do not require input for every mode reset.
The final marked Race attempt contains only a short N-to-D pulse and no recorded subsequent long hold.
Earlier narrow searches included the input pulse in their baseline and missed it; whole-window inspection corrected that false negative.
hypotheses.next_test: Install matched C1/BH 00b4b99 firmware and verify A/D/Race startup selection, release, sustained factory DNA/transmission reports, cancellation and later physical selector use. N must preserve factory behavior.

hypotheses.description: A repeating wiper-associated cycle phase, not a steady rain or enable state. Median message interval 50 ms; slow rising-edge interval about 1500 ms, fast 950 ms. Independent 20261024-111510Z adds 27 pulses and two slow/fast/OFF controls.
contradictions: All three new rain_detected markers fall after a pulse, while this bit is clear. Fixed post-marker occupancy would miss the signal.
One additional pulse at 403.85 s in the old wiper session has no matching wiper marker; it remains unlabelled, not discarded.
hypotheses.next_test: Observe and count physical sweeps alongside phase edges, especially single wipe and fast speed. Do not repeat the full sensor scenario merely to find a trigger.

hypotheses.description: AUTO selection report is separate from the dipped-beam report at b1.6. C2 0x73E carries the same two distinctions. The older auto_low_beam_report label was misleading.
contradictions: September ON/OFF alone confounded switch selection and lit lamps. October daytime AUTO stays set with lamps off.
alternatives: Reported automatic-lighting enabled state rather than exact physical rotary-switch position
hypotheses.next_test: Use AUTO indication as a candidate gate; validate stale-data and physical override handling before actuator implementation.

hypotheses.description: Two separate raw channels react to covering/uncovering the light sensor: usually 6/6 in daylight and 0/0 while covered in the new session. They return before lamp OFF by about 14–20 seconds on the BH clock. The parts describe two channels, not a combined physical value. Independent 20261024-111510Z shows both raw channels falling while lamps remain manually OFF, then AUTO lamp release 14.411/14.474 s after both channels recover. Units and physical source stay unverified.
contradictions: The entire BH 0x738 frame is not a monotonic counter. Other bytes vary for other reasons.
A short channel-2 dip also appears during a spray phase; it does not repeat in all rain trials.
Independent prior sessions contain other baseline values (3/3, 4/5, 0/0), so no universal binary threshold or lux scale is established.
alternatives: ambient or solar-related values relayed by another module
hypotheses.next_test: A raw light-response association is supported. Establish units/source only if a photometric reading is needed; the next feature acceptance gap is lamp actuation, not another complete input scenario.

hypotheses.description: Byte 2 mask 0x60 is not a specific wiper switch or rain signal; it also changes with unrelated lights in the older capture. This frame already contains battery/IBS fields.
contradictions: It switches through all three fog and high-beam trials while C2 0x2EC cycle phase stays clear.
alternatives: electrical-load-associated battery data, exact meaning unresolved
hypotheses.next_test: Exclude this field as a rain/wiper trigger; retain it as a negative control.

hypotheses.description: Short pulses coincide with spraying in the new session, but the older washer-labelled procedure does not reproduce them. Follow-up spray trials reproduce short pulses; older contradictions remain unresolved.
contradictions: The old washer-labelled steps have cycle pulses with b4.4 clear.
A b4.4 excursion occurs during the old high-beam scenario; labels cannot explain whether a coincident stalk action occurred.
alternatives: mislabeled or incompletely executed older steps
hypotheses.next_test: Do not use this bit to suppress washer wipes until physical spray-only and single-wipe controls distinguish it.
